gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a price for any NAS. The cited Synology spec and KB pages list none. ChatGPT's cards put the DS225+ at $429.99 and the DS425+ at $769.99 (Micro Center), but today the makers' own US stores sell 2-bay Intel boxes with 8 GB of RAM for less: UGREEN DXP2800 at $389.99 and TerraMaster F2-425 Plus at $399.49. The cheapest Synology, the DS223j, now supports Btrfs and Snapshot Replication from DSM 7.2-64570, which is enough for a Veeam or Macrium SMB target.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Synology ABB 7.4 spec page (no prices or model list; it only gives concurrency limits), the cited Snapshot Replication spec page and KB backup tutorial (Synology-only, no prices), and the cited ABB requirements KB page, whose fetched copy had no body text. None of the cited or top results name a non-Synology model or give any price. Only ChatGPT's own cards had prices, from a retailer (Micro Center) whose page I could not open (403). Maker-store prices for UGREEN and TerraMaster, and the DS223j's Btrfs support, appear on none of them.
decides: This confirms that for Veeam Agent Free or Macrium Reflect (which only need an SMB share), a $390–400 2-bay Intel box with 8 GB from UGREEN (DXP2800, $389.99) or TerraMaster (F2-425 Plus, $399.49) costs less than ChatGPT's $429.99 DS225+ card. The DS425+ at $769.99 is a 4-bay box for a workload ChatGPT itself called light. The Synology Plus models are worth paying for only if the shopper drops Veeam/Macrium for Active Backup for Business. ABB's limit of 10 concurrent PC backups under 8 GB RAM covers three PCs on a stock 2 GB DS225+. The DS223j (Btrfs + Snapshot Replication, $209.99 on Amazon) is the floor for a Synology SMB target. Its 1 GB RAM and single 1GbE port are the reason it loses. Our page wrongly lists it as having no snapshots (ext4) and must be corrected.
